summary: The approach is right: the builder family now comes from ledger records (delegation, per-checkpoint model) and the trailer is treated as a claim. Three defects in the new logic undo it. (1) runInspect collects the commit's tree SHA, not the commit SHA, so no checkpoint record ever matches and every PR built with aayu build is reported as having an unknown family. (2) BuilderOf treats a PR as covered when any commit is named, not every commit, so a hand-made commit slips through under a recorded family. (3) The lane fallback condition is inverted (lane == ""), so the build lane's family is never a candidate when there is no record. Criteria 2 and 3 are not met as implemented. The tests that would catch these (TestBuilderOf partial-record and no-record cases, TestInspectBuilderFamily honest case) contradict the code.

findings.title: PR commits are listed by tree SHA, so checkpoint records never match
findings.detail: Checkpoint records are keyed by the commit SHA (git rev-parse HEAD in runBuild), but this loop collects each commit's tree SHA. BuilderOf looks up rec.Checkpoints[c] by these values, so it never finds a record, named stays 0, and every non-delegated PR is reported as having an unknown builder family. An honest PR is no longer reported as "builder family <x> (the build record ...)" (criterion 3). The test fixture returns only {"sha": head}, so GetCommit() is nil and the tree SHA is "", which contradicts the honest-case expectation.
findings.fix: Use the commit SHA: commits = append(commits, x.GetSHA()).

findings.title: Coverage requires only one named commit, not every commit
findings.detail: The doc comment, BUILD-PLAN D-4.8c and how-merge-gate.md all say the family is known only when a checkpoint names a model family for every commit. named > 0 accepts a PR where a single checkpoint is recorded and other commits are hand-made with any trailer, so the family is reported as known from a record that does not cover the PR. The !covered branch ('names a model family for %d of %d commits') can then only be reached when named == 0, which the len(recorded)==0 case already handles. TestBuilderOf 'a hand-made commit the record lacks' expects family "" and would fail.
findings.fix: Require full coverage: covered := rec.Receiver != "" && rec.Delegated != "" || len(commits) > 0 && named == len(commits).

findings.title: Inverted lane check: the build lane's family is never added as a candidate
findings.detail: The branch runs only when lane is empty, and add("") is a no-op. With no record the lane family (for example anthropic) is never a candidate, and the note never says 'the build lane's family on the pack's host is ...'. With no trailer either, Candidates is empty and the reviewer can share the builder's actual family, which defeats the different-family rule. Criterion 2 (the verdict names the family used and its source) is not met. TestBuilderOf 'no record: the claim and the lane are candidates' and the TestInspectBuilderFamily no-trailer case expect the lane family.
findings.fix: Change the condition to len(recorded) == 0 && lane != "" && lane != verbs.FamilyHostManaged.

criteria.evidence: builder.go:74-76 appends 'the Aayudha-Model trailer claims <model> (self-reported, unverified)' to the note whenever a claim exists and the family is unknown, and Note() puts it first in the verdict (inspect.go notes prepend). The commit-SHA and lane defects weaken the refusal path, but the verdict states the claim is self-reported.

builder.go:77 runs only when lane == "", so with no trailer and no record the lane family is never named or added. The verdict says 'builder family unknown (...); the reviewers are of none of []' and does not name the family used.
inspect.go:350 collects tree SHAs, so checkpoint records keyed by commit SHA never match. An honest recorded build is reported as unknown instead of 'builder family <x> (the build record ...)'.
